name: NOVA
whatItDoes: Harnesses global compute and collective intelligence to navigate huge unexplored chemical spaces, uncovering candidate drug compounds at a fraction of the usual cost and time.
whatMinerDoes: Miners run the NOVA harness on GPU hardware (the installer's default is CUDA 12.6) pointed at task code pulled from a GitHub repo they configure via env vars (owner/repo/branch/path), plus a validator API key path for validators. The README extract is truncated, so the exact chemistry workloads and scoring are not spelled out here; the on-chain blurb says the subnet accelerates drug discovery. Emission is extremely concentrated: 1 of 64 registered miners is rewarded.
whatValidatorDoes: Runs with a validator API key and auto-update enabled; scoring logic is not shown in the extract.
rewardBasis: drug-discovery task performance (details not in extract)

name: Herald
whatItDoes: A marketplace for verified mainstream-media placement: news articles get published in real outlets, and an automatic code-only oracle verifies each claimed placement on the public web before miners are paid in emissions.
whatMinerDoes: Miners are PR operators and outlet owners, not server operators. They read open briefs, commit a salted hash of (brief_id, outlet, hotkey, nonce, version, evidence) on chain with the outlet hidden until reveal, get the article actually published in a real outlet, then attach the URL and serve the reveal to validators via ClaimSynapse. Rewards release in installments over a 30-day persistence window; if the article disappears the remaining installments are clawed back and the hotkey is slashed. Admission is just the standard non-refundable registration burn - no extra per-claim bond.
whatValidatorDoes: Runs a cheapest-first, early-exit verification oracle per claim (commitment valid, outlet tier, URL live, real-news not paid, topic match, search-index presence) and attributes each article to the earliest valid commit.

The README extract has no explicit miner-setup section, so runtime specifics (hardware, stack) are not documented here - this is a model-submission competition rather than an infrastructure-hosting slot.

rewardBasis: daily Arena model evaluation vs hidden ICPs

name: Gittensor
whatItDoes: Accelerates open-source software development by rewarding meaningful contributions: miners earn TAO for real, merged pull requests to recognized open-source repositories, plus a secondary track that pays for GPU compute time.
whatMinerDoes: Main track: register with a fine-grained GitHub personal access token and contribute to whitelisted open-source repos - when your PRs get merged you earn, scored on code quality, repository allocation, and programming-language factors (human dev work, not a server farm). Compute track: run one command on a GPU box; the agent it starts is the whole miner, the subnet's controller checks the cards, leases them out, and pays per card.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators authenticate GitHub account ownership via the PAT, verify merged contributions, and score them within each repository's configured emission share.

name: Hippius
whatItDoes: Blockchain-backed decentralized cloud: distributed file storage plus VM/app compute, with a Node Metrics RPC API exposing real-time performance and reward data for storage and VM nodes.
whatMinerDoes: Miners run storage/compute nodes in the Hippius network: they pin files (the API tracks, per account, which miner node IDs pinned each file hash) and host virtual machines deployed by accounts (VM records include status, deployment details, and the associated miner). 130 of 256 miners are rewarded, so emission is broadly spread. No explicit miner-setup section is included in the extract.
whatValidatorDoes: Not detailed in the extract; the overview says validators help ensure secure and reliable data management across the network.

name: Ormas
whatItDoes: An Outcomes API for coding work on Bittensor: clients post a change plus the test that proves it, miners quote a firm price for the passing result, and miners are paid only when independent validators accept the delivered branch.
whatMinerDoes: Miners are code-delivery suppliers: they post a firm USD bid (ask_usd) for a whole task, perform the coding work, and deliver a branch through the reference miner ('the runner is the miner'). Payment is exactly the accepted ask - never for inference served, tokens spent, or hardware occupied. The economics are disclosed as planned-not-yet-live, and the operator (Heron Cove LLC) runs its own miner, validator, and settlement gateway (flagged openly in the README).
whatValidatorDoes: Validators re-run the client's acceptance tests on the delivery before anyone is paid, and convert accepted USD targets into SN76 emission weights each epoch using the on-chain alpha price and a published TAO/USD reference.
rewardBasis: accepted coding outcomes at miner's quoted price

name: Liquidity
whatItDoes: Liquidity mining for the Bittensor ecosystem: token holders vote on which liquidity pools get incentivized, and miners who supply liquidity to those pools (e.g., on external chains via Uniswap) earn subnet emissions.
whatMinerDoes: No compute to run: miners register their Bittensor public key linked to an EVM address, then provide liquidity (capital) into voted pools and monitor pool performance and rewards. Earnings track the liquidity you provide, not hardware or serving.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators fetch vote-derived miner weights from the central server (77.creativebuilds.io), can independently recompute the weights locally for verification, and push them on-chain each cycle.

name: Umi
whatItDoes: Develops ASL-to-English translation through endpoint competition: miners run translation model endpoints and compete, while contributors can submit runnable, licensed artifacts that get promoted into successive public baselines.
whatMinerDoes: Miners set up and submit a translation endpoint (docs cover connecting your model, including an Apple Silicon / macOS setup path, so it is not GPU-only) and must apply the current C4 / policy-8 update to stay compliant - an accepted receipt can remain valid while the update rolls out. Endpoint miners may keep their models private; competition intake and on-chain registration are separate steps.
whatValidatorDoes: Runs a validator supervisor service that scores competing endpoints per current bridge rules with finalized-row diagnostics (exact scoring metrics not shown in the extract).

name: MVTRX
whatItDoes: A simulated-market ecosystem: tauos agent-based simulation of automated trading strategies, GenTRX distributed training of a shared order-book generative model, and an off-chain limit-order-book exchange for Bittensor alpha tokens running the same C++ matching engine.
whatMinerDoes: Miners host trading-agent strategies that receive L3 state updates from the simulated order book and respond with order place/cancel instructions; response latency determines the execution delay (and thus slippage) applied to their orders, so miners must be fast, risk-managed, and active. No strict hardware requirements beyond ~1GB RAM per basic instance. Optional GenTRX opt-in: a background thread trains the shared model on an assigned data slice each round (forward/backward pass, compressed gradient) and uploads it to a personal S3 bucket, earning from the training pool alongside the trading pool.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators run the C++ market simulator plus a Python wrapper that forwards state to miners and scores agents on risk-adjusted performance across all simulated realizations; GenTRX-enabled validators also run a gradient server that scores uploaded gradients against held-out data.
rewardBasis: risk-adjusted trading performance in simulation (+ optional gradient quality)
minerWorkType: Trading agent (CPU, latency-sensitive) + optional GPU training

name: OpenRoboto
whatItDoes: An open Bittensor competition for continuously improving robotics vision-language-action (VLA) models and collecting egocentric data, with simulation and real-robot (xArm 6) evaluation tracks run season by season.
whatMinerDoes: Miners train/fine-tune VLA models and submit complete checkpoints through the packaged openroboto CLI (current season: LingBot-VLA 2.0; archived season: pi0.5). The season-1 flow: read the public control.json, download public training data and the base checkpoint, train inside the isolated openpi-runner container, merge any LoRA adapter into the base and export a full checkpoint (openpi JAX params/ or model.safetensors plus norm_stats - bare LoRA is rejected by a CPU pre-check), upload to Hugging Face, pay the evaluation burn, and announce the model commit on chain. Emission split is 15% simulation, 42.5% real pi0.5, 42.5% real LingBot-VLA 2.0; rewarded models must stay public and can be challenged (upheld challenges burn unpaid rewards).
whatValidatorDoes: The repo's weight-setting validator reads control.json, retrieves weights from a read-only evaluation API endpoint, normalizes them, and calls set_weights; real-robot tracks score 7 tasks x 10 trials (70 trials per model) with every scored trial published on video.
rewardBasis: evaluated VLA task success (simulation + real-robot trials)

name: Reliquary
whatItDoes: The RL layer of Bittensor: decentralized GRPO training where independent miners spend their own GPU compute searching for prompts at the policy's learning frontier, and a trainer admits, ranks, verifies, rewards, and trains on the best rollout groups (base model Qwen3-4B-Base).
whatMinerDoes: Miners run the pinned miner Docker image and 'reliquary mine' against a validator URL, choosing any nonempty subset of Math (openmathinstruct), Code (opencodeinstruct), and Logic (reliquary_logic_v2) environments; they generate sixteen trajectories per prompt and submit verified rollout groups within fill-closed windows. You keep your own GPU selection, wallet mounts, miner state directory, and Hugging Face cache; checkpoints rotate automatically (current lineage N1812, Qwen3-4B DAPO) and miners must follow the validator's advertised successor checkpoints. Miners are paid for verified rollout groups the trainer can use - not for raw rollout volume.
whatValidatorDoes: The trainer/validator admits, ranks, verifies (with safety gates and Prime Intellect Verifiers-format environment contracts), rewards, and trains on the best groups - validator-authoritative rewards with public evidence at every boundary.

name: Compelle
whatItDoes: An adversarial-persuasion arena: miners commit written debate strategies on chain, and each epoch the validator pairs miners into Pro/Con LLM debates over a shared topic, scoring outcomes via Elo.
whatMinerDoes: Miners commit a written debate strategy on chain; the validator's LLM debaters then argue Pro/Con using those strategies each epoch. The extract has no explicit miner-setup section, so the practical workload looks like strategy authoring with no serving hardware described. Note only 1 of 64 registered miners is currently rewarded.
whatValidatorDoes: Once per epoch it reads metagraph commitments, filters eligible miners, runs a round-robin tournament of LLM debates, updates Elo, derives weights, calls set_weights, and posts signed epoch results to a public aggregation endpoint.
rewardBasis: Elo ranking of LLM debate outcomes

name: CliqueAI

whatMinerDoes: Miners run the provided miner start script (wallet, axon IP/port on finney) and solve maximum-clique problems; a smart allocation engine filters eligible miners and samples each with the same difficulty-adjusted probability, keeping distribution fair while scaling participation by challenge difficulty. The extract is thin - scoring details and hardware requirements are not documented here.
whatValidatorDoes: Not detailed in the extract beyond the allocation engine; a validator start script is provided.

name: Investing
whatItDoes: Envisioned as the world's first Decentralized AUM: a worldwide network of human and artificial intelligence providing investment services (TAO/Alpha and US large-cap stocks) for retail and institutional investors.
whatMinerDoes: Miners run the standard miner neuron (pm2 + neurons/miner.py); strategy files dropped under Investing/strat/ are automatically submitted, and revising/rebalancing just means updating the file timestamp. US-stock strategies rebalance via Market-on-Open and Market-on-Close orders before the 09:28 / 15:50 ET cutoffs; allocation changes incur slippage, staking/unstaking, and transaction fees. The UID space and emissions are partitioned by asset ratio; each miner needs ~192 Alpha staked + 64 Alpha paid; near-duplicate strategies get reduced scores; one machine can run multiple miners.
whatValidatorDoes: Daily score calculation at 00:00 UTC (TAO/Alpha) and 06:00 UTC (US stocks) on raw performance, with validators producing adjusted rankings and scores that match on-chain incentives.

name: InfiniteQuant
whatItDoes: Proof of Edge for trading signals: miners commit encrypted directional trade calls, validators grade them against real market data, and emissions go to miners with statistically proven edge.
whatMinerDoes: Miners submit hotkey-signed directional calls (e.g., XAUUSD LONG) to wss://hf.infinitequant.app, verify receipts against the published ingest key, and keep local receipt/sequence files as fraud-proofs. Two gates decide payouts: participation (50 accepted submissions across 8 distinct UTC days before wins pay) and direction diversity (a minimum minority-direction share per pair, scaled by pairs traded, or the hotkey earns zero until fixed). Runs on Python 3.10 (timelock dependency); lightweight, no GPU mentioned.
whatValidatorDoes: The authoritative validator journals and grades committed calls against realized market data under a single-validator model with a publicly replayable checkpoint (audit_journal.py re-derives weights; a reseeded validator re-earns qualification over roughly 6-28 observed days).

name: KubeTEE
whatItDoes: The 'AI Factory' of Bittensor: enterprise-grade confidential computing for SOTA AI services (inference, NeMo microservices, retrieval, agents) and batch jobs (fine-tune, eval, pipelines) on decentralized multi-cluster Kubernetes with hardware-secured Trusted Execution Environments.
whatMinerDoes: Miners operate whole Kubernetes clusters, not single boxes: RKE2 (Rancher) with Kata Containers / Confidential Containers TEE runtime, one cluster per miner hotkey, all nodes co-located in a single data center. Minimum for staging participation is 7 nodes (5 combined control-plane/etcd/worker nodes running GPU Operator, Kata/CoCo, Longhorn, NeMo, Armada Executor, monitoring, plus 2+ dedicated 8-GPU workers per GPU type). Onboarding is currently platform-driven - KubeTEE binds your cluster via the kubetee.ai/hotkey label (self-service onboarding is Phase 1) and onboarding rate is demand-driven - plus a 100 TAO registration deposit that freezes on your own hotkey if you breach SLA. Only 3 of 99 miners are rewarded, so emission is extremely concentrated.
whatValidatorDoes: A validator designed to run inside a confidential TEE pod (CoCo remote attestation) scores each miner cluster on a single Infrastructure mechanism - attestations and metrics verified via Rancher Fleet GitOps - and sets weights each epoch; the dashboard is published to Hippius S3 each cycle.
minerWorkType: K8s cluster ops + TEE GPU infrastructure

name: BitSota
whatItDoes: A decentralized research network (on-chain name still 'pending...') that evolves machine-learning algorithms through competitive optimization - problem-agnostic, with a focus on self-improving and self-generating AI.
whatMinerDoes: Three participation modes: Direct mining - run a genetic-programming engine locally for up to 150 generations and submit breakthroughs (higher compute, larger rewards); Pool mining - participants handle smaller evolution/evaluation tasks, the pool aggregates with median consensus (3+ evaluators, 10% tolerance) and submits on their behalf (best for limited compute); and an experimental research-agent mode that can launch an external agent CLI (OpenAI-compatible chat-completions path kept as fallback) across standard, centerless, and peer_evaluation task modes. A desktop GUI from bitsota.ai wraps hotkey import and mode selection.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators run autoresearch replay validation of assigned work and apply backend-directed Bittensor weights (the backend publishes reward_policy.validator_weights; the legacy relay/local validator path has been removed).
